case: Case 2: optical transceivers × FCC Covered List
status_line: Scenario, not forecast. Parameters marked reported have no official text yet.
no_official_text: No official text has been published. These parameters come from press and analyst reporting.

options.label: No transceiver rule
options.note: Component rule only (FCC 26-50), which reaches producer-based Covered List entities and so no transceiver segment here.

options.label: Named companies only
options.note: InnoLight, Eoptolink and subsidiaries, as named in S.5548.

options.label: Chinese-headquartered makers
options.note: Any Chinese-HQ maker, wherever it builds.

options.label: Made in China
options.note: Anything made in China, whoever owns it.

options.label: Either
options.note: Chinese-HQ makers anywhere, plus anything made in China.

options.label: New models only
options.note: Models authorised before the start keep selling.

options.label: Also stop new sales of existing models
options.note: Equipment already installed is never affected.

options.label: Federal systems only
options.note: S.5548 style: federal procurement for national-security systems.

levers.label: Exemption threshold (% of BOM value from US companies)

confidence_resample.note: A lever set by an intel card takes its 'alt' option in this share of simulated futures (DECISIONS #33). Levers set by a preset or by hand are fixed.

cards.headline: Component rule in force: logic-bearing parts from Covered List producers
cards.note: FCC 26-50 applies to new authorisations only. Only producer-based Covered List entries (e.g. Huawei, ZTE) trigger it, so it does not reach InnoLight or Eoptolink optics today.

cards.headline: FCC reported to be drafting a ban on new models of Chinese transceivers
cards.note: Four unnamed sources (Reuters). No FCC threat determination or draft text has been published.

cards.headline: Ban reported to phase in from the 3.2T generation (≈2028–29)
cards.note: From analyst notes of meetings in Washington (Morgan Stanley). Other analysts expect 800G/1.6T revisions to count as new models (PR-012, PR-016).

cards.headline: Possible exemption at ≥65% US bill-of-materials value
cards.note: Economic Daily News citing Morgan Stanley (via TrendForce); a single reported chain. Chinese-assembled modules use US DSPs and US/Japanese lasers (PR-014).

cards.headline: Trigger unsettled: company ownership or place of manufacture?
cards.note: Applying this card keeps 'Chinese-headquartered makers' but treats it as uncertain: in half of simulated futures the rule follows place of manufacture instead, which leaves Thai-made modules outside.

cards.headline: S.5548: federal procurement ban on InnoLight and Eoptolink transceivers (introduced)
cards.note: Introduced and referred to HSGAC, not enacted. The bill's prohibitions take effect five years after enactment; modelled as a phase-in from an assumed 2027 enactment (an upper bound on early effect).

cards.headline: InnoLight added to the Department of War 1260H list
cards.note: Context only: sets no transceiver lever. Entity contracting ban from 30 Jun 2026; product ban from 30 Jun 2027 excludes components inside end items. InnoLight disputes the designation (PR-040).

cards.headline: Power inverters on the Covered List, narrowed to utility-interactive UL 1741 units
cards.note: Context only: drives the power item in the design checklist. Whether data-centre UPS or battery systems fall in scope depends on that definition.

cards.headline: Consumer-grade routers on the Covered List
cards.note: Context only. Residential, customer-installed routers; generally not data-centre networking. Conditional Approvals listed as of 4 Jun 2026 end between 1 Oct and 5 Dec 2027.

presets.label: As reported
presets.blurb: Intel cards I-1 to I-5 applied.

presets.label: Federal systems only (S.5548)
presets.blurb: Named companies, federal buyers, five-year phase-in.

presets.label: By place of manufacture, from 1.6T
presets.blurb: Made in China, 1.6T and faster, no exemption.

presets.label: Widest reach
presets.blurb: Company or place of manufacture, all new models, no exemption, from 2027.

presets.label: No new rule
presets.blurb: Status quo: the component rule only.

timeline.event: Consumer-grade routers added to the Covered List
InnoLight added to the 1260H list (188 entities)
Foreign-produced power inverters added to the Covered List

considerations.title: Manufacturing-site records
considerations.check: Can each optics SKU be tied to a factory location? Thai-made and China-made modules may be treated differently.

considerations.title: BOM provenance
considerations.check: Is there supplier data on the value share of DSPs, lasers and drivers by company nationality, and could it support a 65%-style test?

considerations.title: Architecture timing
considerations.check: 3.2T decisions (pluggable, linear-drive or co-packaged optics) land as the rule starts. Co-packaged optics move the optics into the switch, which changes which equipment authorisation and which components are examined (compare the component rule, I-1).

considerations.title: Second-source qualification
considerations.check: Qualification time is the main lever on delay in this scenario. Which non-covered suppliers are qualified for each generation?

considerations.title: Buy-ahead and inventory
considerations.check: The scenario implies stockpiling before the start year. What is the inventory and obsolescence trade-off?

considerations.title: Separating federal capacity
considerations.check: S.5548 would apply to federal procurement for national-security systems after five years. Does federal capacity need separate optics sourcing?

considerations.title: Installed base
considerations.check: Under a new-models-only rule, modules already installed are not affected. Refresh-cycle timing decides when the rule starts to matter at each site.

considerations.title: Inverters and battery systems
considerations.check: The Covered List entry now covers utility-interactive UL 1741 inverters with remote communications (I-8). Does on-site solar, battery storage or grid-interactive UPS equipment fit that definition, and were models authorised before 28 Jul 2026?

considerations.title: Routers and switches
considerations.check: The router entry is consumer-grade (I-9), so it is unlikely to cover data-centre switching. The component rule (I-1) still applies to any device with logic-bearing parts from producer-based Covered List entities.

considerations.title: Firmware
considerations.check: FCC 26-50 excludes firmware for now and keeps the record open (I-1). A watch item, not a current requirement.
